title: Fitness Criteria Decomposition in ARCHITECT
summary: When ARCHITECT assigns a qualitative claim ("transparent," "seamless," "backward-compatible," etc.) to a module's responsibility, the system-design step requires the claim to be decomposed into one or more testable fitness properties, recorded as `**Fitness:** <observable property> — <how observed/measured>` adjacent to the claim, before the ARCHITECT gate may pass. The qualitative claim is retained as the human-readable summary; the fitness properties are the verification anchors. Fitness properties carry forward into BUILD, becoming Cycle Acceptance Criteria Table entries (ADR-073) or preservation scenarios (ADR-075) where applicable, addressing the ARCHITECT-phase share of the Issue #13 failure chain.
workflow_point: ARCHITECT system-design step — qualitative-claim decomposition gate
mechanism: testable Fitness property statement per qualitative claim; gate refuses to advance when undecomposed

links.note: fitness properties that specify a verification layer become entries in the Cycle Acceptance Criteria Table (ADR-073)

rejects deferring the gate check to a periodic /rdd-conform audit for the same reason ADR-074's Step 3 rejects deferring its check to a periodic sweep — a forcing function at the moment of decision beats a later audit
fitness properties that are scenario-decomposable may become preservation scenarios (ADR-075)

ADR-077's prompt 4 ("Which fitness properties does system-design.md declare for the affected module(s)?") consumes this ADR's decomposed fitness properties, making them load-bearing at the BUILD pattern-reuse moment
